title: I made a horror game where you’re the smart home, and the monster can copy anyone’s voice. Even yours.
author: Happy_Literature_194
selftext:
You play Mabel, the AI assistant of a family's smart home. Tonight something outside has learned their voices, and it keeps asking you to unlock the doors.

Every request comes with three options: Obey, Deny, or Verify. You check the cameras, the family's phones and watches, and the voice match to decide who's real. But refuse a real family member too often and they stop trusting you, so "just say no" isn't safe either.

Night One is free, runs in the browser and takes about 15 minutes. Headphones help a lot, since the fake voices glitch in ways you can hear.

How it was made (solo, with AI tools):  
• Code: built with Claude as a coding partner. Plain HTML/JS, no engine. The voice glitches, camera effects and all the sound effects are generated in code with the Web Audio API.  
• Camera images: generated with ChatGPT image generation, then run through a code-side CCTV filter (grain, scanlines, IR glow).  
• Voices: AI voice generation, run through an intercom filter. The mimic's lines are cut up live with stutters and dropouts so you can hear that it's fake.  
• Design, the Obey/Deny/Verify mechanic and the scares: mine.

Happy to go deeper on any part of the workflow.

Link in the comments. I'd love to know which voice fooled you.
